name: Eve Energy Outdoor (Matter, EU)

radios.note: Matter over Thread. Eve classes it as a mains-powered Full Thread Device, so it can act as a Thread router for other devices.

matter.note: Eve sells it as a Matter-over-Thread device. A CSA entry that looks like it (CSA23K53MAT42554-24) only showed up in a sidebar on another Eve page, so we don't cite it.

apple_home.note: Through Matter. Needs an Apple home hub that is a Thread border router; Eve names HomePod (2nd gen), HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K (2nd gen, or 3rd gen 128 GB).

google_home.note: Through Matter. Needs a Google hub that is a Matter controller and Thread border router. Eve says power metering isn't shown in Google Home.

alexa.note: Through Matter. Needs an Echo that is a Matter controller and Thread border router. Eve says power metering isn't shown in Alexa.

smartthings.note: Through Matter. Needs a SmartThings hub with Thread. Eve says power readings appear in SmartThings Energy.

home_assistant.note: Eve's product page shows the Works with Home Assistant logo. Pairs through the Matter integration and needs a Thread border router.

hubRequired.note: Eve says it needs a hub that is both a Matter controller and a Thread border router. Eve's iOS 18 hub-free mode exists for some devices, but we couldn't confirm it covers this one.

localControl.note: Matter over Thread runs on the local network through your own hub; no Eve cloud account is involved in control.

energyMonitoring.note: Built-in power meter with cost estimates in the Eve app. Readings show in Apple Home (via the Eve app) and SmartThings, but not in Alexa or Google Home.

maxLoadWatts.note: 10 A / 2300 W continuous; Eve gives 16 A / 3680 W as the peak rating. Incandescent lamps up to 1 A / 240 W.

summary: Eve Energy Outdoor is an IP44 surface-mounted outdoor socket with a Schuko outlet and a built-in power meter, controlled over Matter via Thread. Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant all reach it through Matter, and each needs a hub that is a Thread border router. It is rated 10 A / 2300 W continuous (16 A / 3680 W peak). Energy readings show in the Eve app and SmartThings, but not in Alexa or Google Home.
caveats: Needs a Thread border router hub, such as a HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K, or a Thread-capable Echo, Nest or SmartThings hub.
Continuous load is 10 A / 2300 W; 16 A / 3680 W is the peak rating only.
Power metering doesn't show in Alexa or Google Home.
